items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had met "Bull" a few years before when Edgar Courance and I had made friends with a couple of amateur musicians from Hamilton, Ohio, and we would go there for a couple of days every week and play in a small cabaret.

ctx.x: John Williams got homesick for New York and eventually left the band and another sax-player from Louisville named Lester Carr took his place. The next one to leave the band was Hubert Mann. He received an offer to join Speed Webb's orchestra in California, so Rudolph "Bull" Williams, [who] lived in a town not far from Springfield was hired as banjoist.

Rudolph was a very stocky young fellow who had played football at Wilberforce College and because of his big face, big hands and broad shoulders, he was given the name of "Bull". His father was a preacher but "Bull" was everything except religious. I had met "Bull" a few years before when Edgar Courance and I had made friends with a couple of amateur musicians from Hamilton, Ohio, and we would go there for a couple of days every week and play in a small cabaret. After our return from Hamilton, Ontario, I was able to pay Grandma Jackson back the rent I owed her and also pay Rick for the food I had eaten on the cuff before we left for Canada.
